How to read this

Question. Is what I am reading recorded evidence, and how can I check it myself?

Every value is labelled generated, recorded or written, so you can see who produced it. This snapshot was compiled from origin/main b394466 at 2026-10-19 17:45:08 UTC, and the git commands below re-check the order from a clone.

Step 1

Read the labels

+
+

Each value on the other screens carries one of these three labels. The label says who produced the value. Read it before you weigh the value.

+
+
generateda hook or render-trace.mjs wrote it, never an agent producing the code

The compiled-at stamp in the header above is generated.

+
recordeda hook stored an agent's judgement verbatim; the agent can't alter it afterwards

A reviewer or security verdict is recorded: you read the agent's own words, not a summary of them.

+
writtenby David or the main session

Text authored by a person or the main session carries this label. Read it as a claim made by its author, not as a measurement.

+
+
+
+
+ +
+
+

Step 2

Look up the terms

+
+

A status is always a word, a glyph and a colour. Colour is never the only signal.

+
+
Pass

What was counted or checked passed. A count says what it was counted from.

+
Fail

A recorded check or verdict failed. It keeps its own rung and is never folded into a count.

+
Warn

A gap or disagreement in the trail. Read the sentence beside it before relying on the value.

+
Pending

Not done yet, so there is nothing to check yet.

+
Not built

Not built yet. There is no red, green, refactor, QA step or sign-off to show, and the page says so instead of inventing one.

+
+

Terms used on the other screens.

  • Rung. One numbered step in a story. The number is the step's position in the order, not a time.
  • Red, green, refactor. The values of a commit's TDD trailer. A rule page puts the red commit above the green one, so you read the order from position.
  • Attempt. One pass of a node through the build loop. Every attempt keeps its own rung; retries are never folded into a counter.
  • gate.stub. A recorded check, shown with what it expected and what it returned.
  • Verdict. A reviewer's or security agent's PASS or FAIL, recorded verbatim.
  • Finding. A problem a verdict raised. A later commit's Fixes-Finding trailer names the one it fixes.
  • Human decision. A point where David approved, steered or merged. They are listed together on the Human decisions screen.
  • Git-only. A node with no trail files; what is shown comes from git alone.
  • Snapshot. The commit this site was compiled from, stamped in step 5.
+
+
+
+ +
+
+

Step 3

Re-run it in git

+
+

You do not have to trust this site. Each command below runs in a clone and prints what git itself holds. Run them in this order.

+
+

First, confirm the snapshot commit exists.

+

Run this in a clone. It asks git what kind of object the stamp's SHA is.

git cat-file -t b394466f9e89d823fbe13a904ab45296d782b033

Expect commit.

The SHA is the one in the compiled-at stamp (step 5); the page has no recorded output for it.

+
+
+

Then re-check an order. The command lists commits oldest first, each with its TDD trailer. A rule page gives its own red and green SHAs; the two below are the kit's specimen pair, not part of this page's data.

+

Run this in a clone. It lists the commits from the red SHA to the green SHA in the order they were made, with each one's TDD trailer.

git log --reverse --format="%h %(trailers:key=TDD,valueonly) %s" 94a7473^..92ede9e

Expect 94a7473 first with trailer red and 92ede9e last with trailer green.

Specimen SHAs from the kit; swap in the pair from any rule page. The page has no recorded output for this command.

    Symptom
    four SELL-1 accept tests pass on the canned stub. They are New_reference_is_sold_with_201_and_its_Location_and_reads_back (SellReferenceTests.cs:22-29), Policy_sold_reads_back_by_its_reference_in_lower_case (:44-53), Reference_of_3_characters_is_accepted (:99-104) and Reference_of_20_characters_is_accepted (:120-127).
    Cause
    these tests check nothing beyond the shared helper SellAndReadBack (PoliciesClient.cs:43-55). The helper checks 201 (:46), that Location equals /policies/{expected} (:48), GET 200 (:51), and that the read-back reference equals the expected one (:53). The stub can meet every one of those checks with no storage. It builds Location from the request's own reference (PoliciesController.cs:16-17), and the GET builds the body's reference from the route (PoliciesController.cs:21-22, 24-25). So the reference read back is just the route echoed back. The extra asserts at :28 and :52 repeat that echo. The lower-case test does not show that a case-insensitive lookup found the stored row, because the stub upper-cases the route itself (PoliciesController.cs:22). Reference_is_trimmed_and_upper_cased_in_the_Location_and_the_stored_policy (:33-40) has the same weakness. It is red today only because the DTO pattern at SellPolicyRequest.cs:22 rejects surrounding spaces before any trimming, so it gets a 400. Once green fixes that, an echoing stub would pass it too. Rule: 'The client supplies the reference. It is trimmed and upper-cased, then must match ^[A-Z0-9-]{3,20}$ … abc-1 and ABC-1 are the same policy.' Accepted means stored and readable as sold, and these tests never check that.

+# QA script: ui / U4, agents, human decisions and verify-it-yourself: the explorer end to end
+
+Rule IDs: AGENT-1, AGENT-2, HITL-1, VERIFY-1, NAV-2, NAV-4, PERF-1
+Branch: feature/ui/U4   Worktree: .claude/worktrees/ui-U4
+Commit under test: write the SHA you test in the sign-off. This script was written at 792247f (attempt 2 opened),
+while the attempt-2 fix round was landing beside it. Test at the HEAD that carries those fixes, not at 792247f.
+App URL: http://localhost:4175. U4's app port is 4175 and its API port 5085. The explorer needs no API; the
+workbench pages do, so start the API too if you open them.
+
+U4 builds or completes these, all explorer screens read from `trace.json`:
+
+- the commit page's trailer agent against the hook agent, and the node page's `Who touched what` (AGENT-1);
+- the activity page's agent lanes and its text table (`#/plans/<plan>/<node>/activity`) (AGENT-2);
+- the human decisions page (`#/decisions`) and the overview's latest decisions (HITL-1);
+- `Verify it yourself` on the rule page and `Re-verify with git` on the about page (VERIFY-1);
+- a URL for every entity, the not-found page and an open session at `#/sessions/<file>` (NAV-2);
+- the top-bar search over rule IDs, nodes, SHAs and file paths (NAV-4);
+- the cold-load mark and the lazy chunks (PERF-1).
+
+The steps below are written for the behaviour after the attempt-2 fixes:
+
+- a file-path search result opens that file on GitHub, in a new tab, at the snapshot SHA (NAV-4, steps 33 to 35);
+- the activity lanes draw every agent in the log, including `web-tester`, `web-builder` and `kit-builder` (AGENT-2,
+  steps 8 to 10);
+- Enter opens the highlighted search result (NAV-4, step 32);
+- the rule page's git command still lists the red before the green when a merge sits between them (VERIFY-1, step 22);
+- every link out to GitHub carries `rel="noreferrer"` (steps 13, 19, 34).
+
+The Actual and Pass/Fail columns are empty. I wrote these steps from the code and the acceptance suite
+(`tests/web/e2e/U4/`) and didn't run them in the app. The acceptance suite runs on fixture trails; this script runs on
+the real trail at HEAD, so where a count can move, the step gives the command that counts it.
+
+## Run the app on U4's ports
+
+Commands are for Git Bash, run from the worktree root, `.claude/worktrees/ui-U4`.
+
+```sh
+git status --short; git rev-parse HEAD                  # write both down
+npm --prefix src/web run trace                          # the trail at HEAD -> src/web/public/trace.json
+npm --prefix src/web run build
+npm --prefix src/web run preview -- --port 4175 --strictPort   # leave it running; DOCKET_API_PORT=5085 for the workbench
+```
+
+Counts used below, in a second terminal:
+
+```sh
+node -e "const t=require('./src/web/public/trace.json');console.log('decisions',t.decisions.length);t.decisions.forEach(d=>console.log(d.kind,d.who,d.where,d.evidence&&d.evidence.file+':'+d.evidence.line))"
+node -e "const t=require('./src/web/public/trace.json');const c=t.commits.filter(c=>c.plan==='build'&&c.node==='F1');console.log(c.length);c.forEach(c=>console.log(c.short,c.agent,c.hookAgent))"
+for n in build/F1 ui/U1 ui/KG1; do echo "$n: $(grep -o '"agent":"[^"]*"' docs/trace/$n/activity.jsonl | sed 's/"agent"://' | tr -d '"' | awk '!s[$0]++' | tr '\n' ' ')"; done
+node -e "const t=require('./src/web/public/trace.json');const r=t.rules.find(r=>r.id==='SELL-1');console.log(r.red,r.green,r.refactor)"
+ls -la src/web/public/trace.json src/web/public/trace/*/*/                   # the index and its lazy chunks
+```

Docket: concept

David adopted the territory's governing idea unchanged as the concept. What the territory refuses and the category default it departs from are its excludes and categoryDeparture in docs/ui/directions.json.

On this page

  1. Concept
  2. The proposition
  3. What the territory refuses
  4. Layout
  5. Tone
  6. Type: T5, licence checked

Concept

Order is the proof: every story the app tells (a rule going red then green, an attempt failing then being fixed, a quote leading to a cancel) is a numbered sequence read top to bottom, and nothing can be read out of turn.

The governing idea was written by the creative-director agent, and David adopted it as his concept. It was not written by him; this is recorded for EFF-9.

The proposition

What the territory refuses

  1. A two-axis matrix as the way into a story: the rule page and the cancel screen read down one spine, and the matrix is only an index.
  2. Wall-clock time axes, waterfalls and duration bars: position is ordinal (#1, #2, ...), because the walkthrough and matrix carry commit order, not commit dates, and API responses carry no timestamps.
  3. Side-by-side panes and tabs that let a story's steps be read out of order.
  4. Folding retries into a counter or a passing summary: every attempt keeps its own rung.
  5. Asking the user to re-enter a value a later step depends on: the quoted date is carried down, not typed again.

Layout

Single vertical spine of numbered rungs: an ordinal rail down the page with each step's label to its left and its receipt to its right; retries step off to the side and rejoin the spine; the keyboard moves rung to rung with the keys shown; at 390 wide the rail moves to the left edge and receipts stack under their labels.

Tone

Procedural and stepwise: a numbered protocol with short imperative step labels, one thing at a time.

Docket: concept

David adopted the territory's governing idea unchanged as the concept. What the territory refuses and the category default it departs from are its excludes and categoryDeparture in docs/ui/directions.json.

On this page

  1. Concept
  2. The proposition
  3. What the territory refuses
  4. Layout
  5. Tone
  6. Type: T5, licence checked

Concept

Order is the proof: every story the app tells (a rule going red then green, an attempt failing then being fixed, a quote leading to a cancel) is a numbered sequence read top to bottom, and nothing can be read out of turn.

The governing idea was written by the creative-director agent, and David adopted it as his concept. It was not written by him; this is recorded for EFF-9.

The proposition

What the territory refuses

  1. A two-axis matrix as the way into a story: the rule page and the cancel screen read down one spine, and the matrix is only an index.
  2. Wall-clock time axes, waterfalls and duration bars: position is ordinal (#1, #2, ...), because the walkthrough and matrix carry commit order, not commit dates, and API responses carry no timestamps.
  3. Side-by-side panes and tabs that let a story's steps be read out of order.
  4. Folding retries into a counter or a passing summary: every attempt keeps its own rung.
  5. Asking the user to re-enter a value a later step depends on: the quoted date is carried down, not typed again.

Layout

Single vertical spine of numbered rungs: an ordinal rail down the page with each step's label to its left and its receipt to its right; retries step off to the side and rejoin the spine; the keyboard moves rung to rung with the keys shown; at 390 wide the rail moves to the left edge and receipts stack under their labels.

Tone

Procedural and stepwise: a numbered protocol with short imperative step labels, one thing at a time.

Type: T5, licence checked

Both faces are OFL-1.1 in their Google Fonts builds, so they can be self-hosted from a public repo. The research's "EULA" was the Braille Institute's own download; the kit uses the Google Fonts OFL builds, and their OFL.txt ships beside the font files.

Still open before G3

Tabular figures in both faces: neither page states them. The kit's specimen test settles it.

Single vertical spine of numbered rungs: an ordinal rail down the page with each step's label to its left and its receipt to its right; retries step off to the side and rejoin the spine; the keyboard moves rung to rung with the keys shown; at 390 wide the rail moves to the left edge and receipts stack under their labels.

Tone

Procedural and stepwise: a numbered protocol with short imperative step labels, one thing at a time.

Type: T5, licence checked

Both faces are OFL-1.1 in their Google Fonts builds, so they can be self-hosted from a public repo. The research's "EULA" was the Braille Institute's own download; the kit uses the Google Fonts OFL builds, and their OFL.txt ships beside the font files.

Still open before G3

Tabular figures in both faces: neither page states them. The kit's specimen test settles it.
